answer: Put next year's money into retention, aimed at small clinics: churn rose from 4% [F1] to 7% [F2] after the March release, and the extra churn costs $30,600 [F14] of monthly recurring revenue every month.
exec_summary: Monthly logo churn rose by 3 points [F11], and net revenue retention fell from 104% [F3] to 96% [F4].
Clinics with fewer than ten staff make up 70% [F8] of churned logos; they onboard alone and hit the March release hardest.
Price is what churned clients say, but a discount saves only 15% [F9] of cancellations, so price is the stated reason rather than the cause.
Restoring churn to 4% [F10] recovers about 26 [F13] clinics a month, worth $30,600 [F14] in monthly recurring revenue each month.
situation: A B2B scheduling platform for clinics with 850 [F5] customers paying on average $1,200 [F6] per month.
complication: Within two quarters monthly churn rose from 4% [F1] to 7% [F2], and support tickets per account doubled after the March release.
key_question: What is driving the churn increase, and should next year's budget go to retention or to new sales?

titles.situation: Churn nearly doubled in two quarters while the customer base stayed the same size.
titles.options: Three ways to respond, and only one fits the hiring and engineering limits.
titles.recommendation: Fund a small-clinic retention program before adding sales capacity.
titles.roadmap: Ninety days to prove the program on small clinics, then extend it.
titles.kpis: Track four measures monthly so the board sees progress early.
titles.risks: The main risks are a misread cause and a stretched support team.

issue_tree.finding: Small clinics drive the increase, not the customer base as a whole.
points: Clinics with fewer than ten staff are 70% [F8] of churned logos.
At 7% [F2] churn the company loses about 60 [F12] clinics a month.

hypotheses.text: Churn is concentrated in a segment rather than spread evenly.
Larger clinics are churning at the new, higher rate too.

issue_tree.finding: The March release made the product harder to use for clinics that onboard alone.
points: Support tickets per account doubled after the March release.
Onboarding is fully self-serve, so small clinics absorb the change without help.

hypotheses.text: The March release raised the effort of daily use.
Self-serve onboarding leaves small clinics without a fallback.

issue_tree.finding: Price is the stated reason for leaving, but discounts barely change the decision.
points: 60% [F7] of churned accounts cite a cheaper tool.
The cancellation discount saves only 15% [F9] of requests.

hypotheses.text: A lower price would win most churning clinics back.
Cheaper tools feel easier, so price stands in for effort.

options.name: Small-clinic retention program
options.description: Guided onboarding and a staffed save desk for clinics under ten staff, using the two allowed hires.

options.name: Deeper cancellation discounts
options.description: Raise the cancellation discount and add an annual-plan discount.

options.name: Shift budget to new sales
options.description: Hire sales capacity and accept current churn while acquisition grows the base.

recommendation.rationale: It targets the segment behind 70% [F8] of churned logos, attacks the effort problem the March release created, needs no engineering in Q1, and fits within two hires; new sales would refill a base that is losing $30,600 [F14] of monthly recurring revenue each month.

actions: Hire a small-clinic success lead and a save-desk specialist.
Call every small clinic that opened a support ticket since the March release.
Replace the discount-only offer with a guided save conversation.
Launch a guided onboarding call for every new small clinic.
Measure the save rate weekly against the planning assumption of 25% [F15].
Decide with the board whether to extend the program to all clinics.
Hand the product team the top support issues for the Q2 roadmap.

kpis.name: Small-clinic churn
kpis.target: Falls faster than overall churn every month

kpis.name: Support tickets per account
kpis.target: Back to the level before the March release

risks.risk: Price, not effort, turns out to be the real driver.
risks.mitigation: Track the reasons given on saved and lost accounts in the first month and revisit the discount if effort fixes do not move churn.

risks.risk: Two hires cannot cover every small clinic.
risks.mitigation: Prioritise clinics with open support tickets and automate the onboarding call script.
